note: Block In Page Not Found provides a single block visibility Condition plugin, page_not_found_request ('Page not found'), with one boolean setting page_not_found (checkbox 'Show in page not found'). When true, evaluate() returns TRUE only on requests with a 404 exception; when false it returns TRUE always. It is stored on the block config entity at visibility.page_not_found_request.page_not_found. No settings page, permissions, services or drush. Cases are grounded in that real block visibility config: introspection reads back that a placed block is restricted to 404s; execution places a block whose visibility uses the condition, verified against the live block config entity.

evals.prompt: On a Drupal 11 site with block_in_page_not_found enabled, how do I make a block appear only on the 404 / page-not-found page?
evals.expected_output: Place the block via Structure > Block layout, then in the block's Visibility settings open the 'Page not found' tab and tick 'Show in page not found'. This uses the page_not_found_request condition, stored at visibility.page_not_found_request.page_not_found = true on the block config.

evals.prompt: What is the machine id of the block visibility condition that block_in_page_not_found provides, and which setting key stores the on/off value?
evals.expected_output: The Condition plugin id is page_not_found_request (label 'Page not found'); its boolean setting is page_not_found, stored under the block's visibility.page_not_found_request.page_not_found.

evals.prompt: For block_in_page_not_found's 'Page not found' condition, what does it evaluate to when the checkbox is on versus off, and how does it detect a 404?
evals.expected_output: When page_not_found is on (1), evaluate() returns TRUE only if the current request has an exception whose status code is 404; when off it returns TRUE unconditionally (no restriction). It adds the url.path cache context and supports negate.

evals.prompt: This Drupal site has a placed block with id bipnf_probe. Inspect its live configuration and state whether it is restricted to the 404 page, naming the visibility condition responsible.
evals.expected_output: Yes, it is restricted to 404s: block.block.bipnf_probe has visibility.page_not_found_request.page_not_found = true (condition id page_not_found_request, 'Page not found').

evals.prompt: This Drupal site has a placed block with id bipnf_neg that uses block_in_page_not_found's 'Page not found' condition. Inspect its live visibility configuration and state whether the condition is negated (i.e. whether the block is hidden on the 404 page rather than shown only on it).
evals.expected_output: The condition is negated: block.block.bipnf_neg has visibility.page_not_found_request with page_not_found = true and negate = true, so the block shows everywhere EXCEPT the 404 page.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site (default theme olivero), place a block with machine id bipnf_hide and configure it, using block_in_page_not_found, so that it appears on every page EXCEPT the 404 / page-not-found page. Apply the change to the live site. You may use the 'Powered by Drupal' (system_powered_by_block) block.
evals.expected_output: A block.block.bipnf_hide config entity exists whose visibility.page_not_found_request has page_not_found = true and negate = true (the 'Show in page not found' condition is enabled and negated), so the block is hidden only on 404 responses.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site (default theme olivero), place a block with machine id bipnf_task and configure it, using block_in_page_not_found, so that it is only visible on the 404 / page-not-found page. Apply the change to the live site. You may use the 'Powered by Drupal' (system_powered_by_block) block.
evals.expected_output: A block.block.bipnf_task config entity exists with visibility.page_not_found_request.page_not_found = true (condition id page_not_found_request), so the block only renders on 404 responses.
